chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-Ahwazi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A white rooster with a split comb guards its little house and seven little houses around it, and a single wing-flutter from a speckled pigeon is superior to seven white roosters with split combs.

key_terms.أَفْرَقُ: A rooster with a split or bifurcated comb — considered especially virtuous in this tradition
key_terms.دُوَيْرَة: A small house or dwelling (diminutive of dar)
key_terms.نَفْضَة: A quick shake or flutter, specifically of wings

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the virtues of a white rooster with a split comb?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the spiritual protective virtue attributed to a white rooster with a split comb (al-afraqu), which is said to guard not only its immediate dwelling but also seven surrounding homes. He further asserts that a single movement or wing-flutter from a speckled pigeon surpasses even the combined protective power of seven such roosters. This hadith reflects a genre of early Islamic wisdom literature in which Imams attributed spiritual and apotropaic properties to specific animals, reflecting beliefs that were culturally widespread in the ancient Near East about animals as protectors of homes.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, form Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Al Qasim Bin Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy, from Muhammad Bin Makhlad Al Ahwazy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A white frightening rooster protects its house and seven houses around it, and a swishing (of the wings) from a speckled pigeon is superior than seven white frightening roosters’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd from al-Qasim ibn ‘ Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimiy from Muhammad ibn Mukhallad al-Ahwaziy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A white rooster which is called afraq protects its house and seven houses around it, however, a vibration from a spotted pigeon is better than seven white roosters.”’
